body: The Tremont Street Subway opened on September 1, 1897 as the first subway in the United States.
The Green Line trunk under Tremont Street is the oldest subway tunnel in North America.
Boston Common, established in 1634, is generally regarded as the oldest city park in the United States.
The Boston Marathon, first run in 1897, is the world's oldest annual marathon.
Fenway Park opened in 1912 and is the oldest ballpark still used in Major League Baseball.
Union Oyster House has served customers since 1826 and calls itself America's oldest continuously operating restaurant.
The Boston Public Library, founded in 1848, was the first large free municipal library in the United States.
The Blue Line crosses under Boston Harbor through the East Boston Tunnel, which opened in 1904 as one of the first underwater transit tunnels in North America.
The Red Line reached Harvard Square in 1912.
The Public Garden, opened in 1837, is home to the Swan Boats, which have paddled its pond since 1877.
The Make Way for Ducklings statues in the Public Garden honor Robert McCloskey's 1941 children's book.
Two lanterns hung in the steeple of Old North Church on April 18, 1775 to signal the British route.
The USS Constitution was launched in 1797 and is the oldest commissioned warship still afloat.
The Bunker Hill Monument is 221 feet tall and has 294 steps to the top.
The Boston Tea Party took place on December 16, 1773.
Faneuil Hall opened in 1742 and is nicknamed the Cradle of Liberty.
The Massachusetts State House dome is covered in 23-karat gold leaf.
The Orange Line ran on the elevated Washington Street structure until it closed in 1987.
Back Bay was filled in from tidal flats starting in 1857.
The Paul Revere House, built around 1680, is the oldest remaining building in downtown Boston.
The Granary Burying Ground is the resting place of Paul Revere, Samuel Adams and John Hancock.
Copp's Hill Burying Ground, established in 1659, is the second oldest burying ground in Boston.
Boston City Hall opened in 1968 and is one of the best-known examples of Brutalist architecture in the country.
South Station opened in 1899 and was once the busiest railroad terminal in the world.
Boston Latin School, founded in 1635, is the oldest public school in the United States.
